name: Gulay
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: A.T.P.L.G. 2012 phonology (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description, not online). Keegan et al. 2014 Lexique Gulay PDF read (morkegbooks.com): tone-marked entries but no stress/prosody statement.

readall_conflicts: Neither work says anything about Gulay itself, so there is no conflict about Gulay. The two do disagree about the sister variety Mbay: Tucker & Bryan 1966 (Bongo-Bagirmi chapter, main language of comparison Sara Mbai, from Stevenson's and Tucker's MSS) give stress normally on the first syllable of disyllables, while Chabrelie 1935 (Mbay of Moissala and Kaba of Makounda, colonial-doctor notes) says the accent is on the last sounded syllable, yet his own examples carry acute marks on first syllables (Gúmbali, kúmda, ádem, úla, lókinge), which fits Tucker & Bryan's initial placement or a tone mark rather than his rule. Both sources predate the tonal analyses (three level tones, Keegan 2014 already held by the project for Gulay) and treat prominence impressionistically.

sources.citation: Chabrelie, Louis. 1935. Notes sur la langue des Sara, avec un vocabulaire comparatif des différents dialectes. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 5(2): 125-151.
sources.note: Open on Persée but the PDF is behind an altcha challenge; a comparative Sara vocabulary that may include Goulaye and an early remark on accent. Low value (1935 amateur notes).

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. n.d. Extended Bibliography (Sara-Bagirmi Language Project), 7 pp.
sources.note: Bibliography only; lists no Gulay-specific work at all (no hit for Gulay/Goulaye/Gulei); Sara-group phonology items are for Mbay, Sar, Ngambay, Gor, Bediondo, Nar, Laka.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Gulay language'; Glottolog 5.x languoid page gula1268
sources.note: Wikipedia gives only an alphabet table (dialects Gulay and Pen); Glottolog page cites only Djarangar 2000 and Ethnologue. Neither says anything about stress.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 2014. The Central Sara Languages, 9th ed. (The Sara Language Project). Cuenca: Morkeg Books. 505 pp. [Glottolog ref 309963 lists the 2012 2nd ed.]
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. General 'Transcription for the Sara Languages' pp. 6-15: three level tones H/M/L on vowels and final sonorants, complex tones on VV and V+sonorant, syllable types CV/CVC (p. 10, 12). 'Introduction to the Gulay Lexicon' pp. 197-199 ('Comments on the Phonology', 'Vowel Patterns', 'Sound Changes') covers consonants, vowel harmony and tone loss before vowel/nasal suffixes; no word 'stress'/'accent' anywhere except in glosses.

sources.citation: Ngaradoumbaye Clément, Nadjirissengar Moise & John M. Keegan. 2014. Lexique Gulay, 5e éd. Cuenca: Morkeg Books. 135 pp. (Glottolog ref 308546)
sources.note: Two-page French introduction (location, speaker numbers, classification, acknowledgement of Jim Roberts for 'problèmes phonologiques'), then abbreviations and the tone-marked lexicon; no phonology section, nothing on stress or tone.
